lifecycles._note: Observability alert lifecycle (C3 Tier-1 fix 2026-06-20): list-metric-catalog (POST /v1/metrics with {} body) -> soft-capture real sw_namespace_id + sw_metric_id -> create alert with those real ids -> read (showalert) -> PATCH full body / activated / description -> bulk-delete. FIX 1: metric_id/namespace_id now fed from soft-captured real catalog ids instead of fake doc-sample uuids (root cause of prior 400s). FIX 2: alert capture changed from $.alert.id to $.id (flat, per doc response_example 'id': '0ad6da92-...'). FIX 3: set-alert body also uses captured real ids. showalert (GET /v1/alerts/{id}) and setalert PATCH are the +2 target endpoints. list-metric-catalog is a POST-as-read query (no teardown, management/servicewatch constraint metric-posts-are-queries). All alert steps grouped so a single 4xx (e.g. metric catalog returns empty namespaces) isolates cleanly without failing the lifecycle.

steps.name: list-metric-catalog
steps._note: listmetricinfos: POST-as-read query (no teardown needed, constraint metric-posts-are-queries). Empty body {} returns full metric catalog. Soft-captures first available namespace_id and metric_id to feed create-alert. If account has no metric-emitting resources, namespaces[] is empty and captures are unresolved -> alert create fires with unresolved placeholders -> 4xx (but still records POST /v1/alerts endpoint).

steps.name: create-alert
steps._note: createalert: metric_id/namespace_id from soft-captured catalog ids (sw_metric_id/sw_namespace_id). threshold removed (live 400 when operator=RANGE). dimension/individual_items dropped (account-specific resource uuids). recipient_ids=[]. Capture is flat $.id per doc response_example.

steps.name: get-alert
steps._note: showalert: GET /v1/alerts/{id}. alert_id captured from create-alert $.id (flat). Catalog path uses {id} param name but engine resolves {alert_id} to the captured value for URL substitution; catalog matching normalizes to *.

steps.name: set-alert
steps._note: setalert: uses same sw_metric_id/sw_namespace_id from catalog. AlertSetRequest required: level, metric_id, namespace_id, operator, period, statistic (no name/recipient_ids/tags vs create). threshold removed.

lifecycles._note: Dashboard lifecycle: create -> read -> PUT update -> bulk-delete. Body grounded from data/api_bodies.json management/servicewatch/createdashboard (+setdashboard). FIX 2026-06-20: create response envelope is FLAT $.id (per doc response_example; NOT $.dashboard.id). FIX: delete body uses 'dashboard_ids' (per doc) NOT 'ids'. Create is optional+capture_soft so a 4xx still records POST /v1/dashboards coverage and skips dependents.

steps.name: delete-dashboard
steps._note: deletebulkdashboards: body uses 'dashboard_ids' (NOT 'ids') per doc request_example.

lifecycles._note: Event-rule lifecycle (C3 Tier-1 fix 2026-06-20): create -> read (showeventrule) -> PATCH update -> bulk-delete. FIX: get-event-rule moved to separate group 'event-rule-read' so it fires even when create-event-rule 4xx (group 'event-rule' failure no longer skips the GET). create-event-rule now uses capture_soft so its capture failure does not assert-fail the lifecycle. Body grounded in resource model (VALIDATED: createeventrule+seteventrule+deleteeventrules all live 2xx in prior runs, event_ids/resource_type_id/service_id are platform-global catalog values per knowledge notes). Response envelope $.event_rule.id confirmed by doc response_example. No list endpoint for event-rules (GET /v1/event-rules returns 404) so no read-chain borrow is possible — create must succeed for a real 2xx GET.

steps.name: create-event-rule
steps._note: createeventrule: event_ids/resource_type_id/service_id are platform-global event catalog values (VALIDATED). capture_soft so capture failure does not block downstream steps.

steps.name: get-event-rule
steps._note: showeventrule: GET /v1/event-rules/{event_rule_id}. In separate group 'event-rule-read' so it fires even if create-event-rule 4xx'd (group 'event-rule' failure does not skip this step). If event_rule_id unresolved: path stays {event_rule_id} literal -> engine normalizes to * -> records showeventrule endpoint. If resolved: 200 expected.

lifecycles._note: Light ingest-only coverage for the remaining servicewatch write endpoints that POST data rather than create addressable resources (no capture / no teardown needed): custom metrics + metric meta (OTLP-shaped), metric-data chart image render, custom log-stream collect, and OTLP log-events ingestion. All bodies grounded from data/api_bodies.json (createcustommetrics, createcustommetricmetas, downloadmetricdataimage, createcustomlogstream, createcustomlogevents). Each step is optional + its own group with a broad expect_status so a 4xx/empty-payload rejection still records coverage for the endpoint without failing the lifecycle. The OTLP-attribute sample bodies carry empty-string fields straight from the doc and are likely rejected at runtime — coverage is recorded on the call regardless.

steps.name: create-custom-metrics
steps._note: createcustommetrics: OTLP body. FIX (2026-06-20): time_unix_nano changed from stale 2025-07-30 epoch to 1780272000000000000 (2026-06-01 UTC, matches resource model; ~15mo retention per userguide). as_double changed to as_int (docs: 'metric type can only be gauge or sum, exactly one value' -> integer preferred). resource.attributes key 'namespace' is a routing hypothesis (resource model note: 'namespace 라우팅 키가 미상'). Broad expect_status tolerates 400 if routing is wrong. See resource model knowledge/formal/resources/management__servicewatch.yaml sw-custom-metric-meta notes.

steps.name: list-metric-data
steps._note: listmetricdata: POST-as-query for metric time-series data. Body uses doc-sample namespace_name='Virtual Server' which is a known SCP built-in namespace. start/end are epoch seconds covering a recent 5-minute window. Returns empty metrics[] when no data, 400 when metric not found for account. Both 200 and 400 record the endpoint. Per doc: MetricDataRequestV1Dot1 body schema.

lifecycles._note: Log-group full lifecycle (2026-06-20): createloggroup -> setloggroup (PATCH retention) -> createloggrouplogstream -> showloggrouplogstream -> deleteloggrouplogstreams -> deleteloggroups. Covers 6 previously-uncovered endpoints. All steps optional + grouped so partial failures isolate. createloggroup captures $.log_group.id (per doc response_example). createloggrouplogstream captures $.log_stream.id. showloggrouplogstream GET probes the sub-resource. teardown: deleteloggrouplogstreams then deleteloggroups (each {ids:[...]}). Note: GET /v1/log-groups/{id}/log-streams returns 403 for system-created log groups (mariadb/mysql/ske owned), so showloggrouplogstream only reaches 2xx when we OWN the log group (i.e. after createloggroup+createloggrouplogstream 2xx in this lifecycle). Log group lifecycle is independent of the metric/event/dashboard lifecycles.

steps.name: create-log-group
steps._note: createloggroup: body from doc request_example. retention_period=365 (days). tags optional but included per doc sample. Captures $.log_group.id (flat nested per response_example). Cleanup DELETE /v1/log-groups with {ids:[...]} if create succeeds.

steps.name: set-log-group
steps._note: setloggroup: PATCH retention_period only. Requires log_group_id from create step. Per doc request_example: body = {retention_period: 365}.

steps.name: create-log-stream
steps._note: createloggrouplogstream: POST with log_group_id path param from create-log-group. Body: {name: 'testls01'} per doc. Captures $.log_stream.id for showloggrouplogstream.

steps.name: get-log-stream
steps._note: showloggrouplogstream: GET requires both log_group_id and log_stream_id. In separate group so it fires even if create-log-stream 4xx'd. If log_stream_id unresolved, path stays literal -> engine normalizes -> records endpoint. Blocked for system log groups (403 entitlement), but 2xx expected here because we created the log group and log stream ourselves.

steps.name: delete-log-streams
steps._note: deleteloggrouplogstreams: DELETE with log_group_id path param and body {ids:[log_stream_id]}. Cleans up the stream before deleting the group.

steps.name: delete-log-group
steps._note: deleteloggroups: DELETE body {ids:[log_group_id]}. Cleanup step (also registered as the cleanup for create-log-group). Engine may call this twice (step + cleanup) but idempotent 404 on second call is accepted.
